name: llama.cpp
tagline: llama.cpp is LLM inference in C/C++
description: llama.cpp is LLM inference in C/C++. Open-source software; the repository lists the licence as MIT.
features: Open-source LLM inference written in C/C++
strengths: Source code and licence are public in the official repository
No licence fee for the software itself
limitations: You run and maintain it yourself, so hosting, hardware and support costs are your own
We have not run or benchmarked it

openSource.note: The official repository lists the licence as MIT

free.details: The software is free to use under its MIT licence; infrastructure and any hosted offerings are separate.

plans.name: Self-hosted (open source)
plans.note: Free software under the MIT licence; your own hosting and hardware costs apply

pricing.regional: No vendor price list. Any hosted or commercial offering from the same team is priced separately and is not covered here.

verification.notes: Project active (LLM inference in C/C++; about 132.8k stars; recent commits). MIT license shown. No pricing: open-source software.
verification.method: Opened in the Claude desktop built-in browser; page text read

profile.headline: Run language models on your own hardware with plain C/C++

capabilities.title: Run models locally or in the cloud
capabilities.text: The project's stated aim is LLM and VLM inference with minimal setup and strong performance across a wide range of hardware.

capabilities.title: Fit larger models in less memory
capabilities.text: Integer quantisation from 1.5-bit to 8-bit speeds up inference and lowers memory use.

capabilities.title: Use CPU and GPU together
capabilities.text: Hybrid inference partly accelerates models that are larger than the GPU's memory.

capabilities.title: Serve an API
capabilities.text: An OpenAI-compatible API server and a built-in web UI are included.

featureCards.name: Apple silicon support
featureCards.text: A first-class target, using ARM NEON, Accelerate and Metal.

featureCards.name: x86 and RISC-V
featureCards.text: AVX, AVX2, AVX512 and AMX on x86; several RISC-V extensions.

featureCards.name: Many GPU backends
featureCards.text: CUDA, HIP, MUSA, Vulkan, SYCL, OpenCL and WebGPU.

featureCards.name: Command-line tools
featureCards.text: cli, completion, server and GBNF grammars.

featureCards.name: Multimodal use
featureCards.text: Shown with a vision-language model session in the CLI.

audienceDetail.who: People who want to run models offline
audienceDetail.text: Local inference with small setup is the project's goal. The page does not name an audience, so these groups follow from what it documents.
The server speaks an OpenAI-compatible API.
The page invites pull requests and lists maintainers and collaborators.

scenarios.title: Run a model straight from Hugging Face
scenarios.text: Use the CLI with a Hugging Face model name.

scenarios.title: Launch a local API server
scenarios.text: Start the server and point an OpenAI-style client at it.

scenarios.title: Chat in the built-in web UI
scenarios.text: Use the browser interface that ships with the server.

scenarios.title: Try a vision-language model
scenarios.text: The page shows a VLM session in the CLI.

gettingStarted.text: Use the install script, visit llama.app, use Docker, download a pre-built binary, or build from source.
Run the CLI with a Hugging Face model, for example a small Qwen GGUF model.
Launch the API server with the same model.
